summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(c) read with Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, and applicable provisions of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access to the InterState Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 and the CERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 seeking revision of Effective Date of 100 MW General Network Access granted in favour of Petitioner Order in Petition No. 83/MP/2025 1 The instant Petition has been filed under Section 79(1)(c) read with Section 79(1)(f) of the Electricity Act, 2003, and applicable provisions of the CERC (Connectivity and General Network Access to the Inter-State Transmission System) Regulations, 2022 and the CERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2023 seeking revision of the Effective Date of 100 MW General Network Access granted to the Petitioner. - _e. Pass such other and further order(s) that this Hon’ble Commission may feel in the interest of justice and the facts and circumstances of the case._ - _f. Condone any error/ omission and to grant an opportunity to the Petitioner to rectify the same;_ - g. _Permit the Petitioner to make such further submission(s), addition(s) and alternation(s) to this Petition as may be necessary from time to time.”_ - **a)** Hindalco Industries Limited (“Petitioner/HIL”) has approached this Commission, being aggrieved by the letter dated 23.09.2024 (“Impugned Letter”) issued by Respondent No. 1 herein, Central Transmission Utility of India Limited (“R-1/CTU”). CTU has rejected the Petitioner’s request (submitted vide letter dated 24.08.2024) for revision of the Effective Date of the 100MW General Network Access (“GNA”) granted by CTU in favour of the Petitioner with respect to the Petitioner’s aluminium project at Mahan, Dist. Singrauli, Madhya Pradesh. He further submitted that CTUIL has acted in accordance with the Order in Petition No. 83/MP/2025 5 **5.** The Petitioner vide note of arguments dated 12.05.2025 has reiterated the earlier submissions and has submitted as follows : Order in Petition No. 83/MP/2025 6 **7.** During the course of the hearing, the Petitioner and the representative of the Respondent, CTUIL, made detailed submissions and concluded their arguments on the maintainability of the Petition. Based on their request, the Commission permitted both sides to file their written submissions/notes of arguments. Subject to the above, the Commission reserved the matter for order. - **a)** The Petitioner is seeking revision in the effective date of GNA from 01.07.2025 to 01.01.2027 on account of the following reasons: - **b)** CTU during the course of argument on 19.05.2025 had averred that it had erroneously stated in the Final Grant that the GNA is granted with network augmentation when in fact, under the GNA Regulations, augmentation is only of the common transmission system. The contention of the CTU that under the GNA Regulations, augmentation is only of the common transmission system is not borne out by a plain reading of the GNA Regulations. The said contentions were raised by CTU only in the Impugned Letter. Even assuming without admitting the contentions of CTU, it is submitted that where the statutory framework is ambiguous or unclear, an entity cannot be held liable to suffer the consequences. Regulatory uncertainty ought not result in hardship to the Petitioner. Furthermore, the Petitioner should not be penalised for the error admittedly committed by CTU. **9.** We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondent and perused the information available on record. **14.** We have considered the submission of the Petitioner and the Respondent. The LILO of VIndhyachal -Sasan at HINDALCO is a dedicated transmission line which was under the scope of the Petitioner and which the Petitioner itself decided to get constructed by PGCIL as per their mutually agreed timelines, tariff, and terms and conditions.
